chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: Occasional singing at parties and the basketball team dances
summary: She sang at parties and after basketball games with a piano in the gym.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Now, you made occasional appearances as a singer over this long period up until the mid-30s.
Do you remember where and what kinds of places you went to --

Around Homestead maybe they'd have a party or cabaret night. You know, cabaret night and I would show up and sing a few songs. There was a group around that had a basketball team. We got involved in . . .
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

We had this basketball team. As you must realize, most of this time we're talking about is during the depression so things were pretty bad around. And so, a lot of young people didn't have very much to do so we got some of the boys together and they formed a basketball team, and then some of the girls got together and formed a basketball team. I was a member of the team. And we rented a little store front just big enough to put a miniature court in there.
Yeah, not good but I just wanted to get into a uniform.

And after our basketball game, we managed to have a piano in the gym. We called it our gym, and of course this is when I did a lot of singing, like after our basketball games. The girls would play the preliminaries and the boys would play the main game, and after the games, why we would have, what we called a dance or something like that, piano. If there was a
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

drummer around we'd get a drummer. This is when I did most of my singing, you know. And this is just, I'm trying to get to the place where I really thought I was, you know, a singer, because I just didn't pay very much attention to singing as a career. To me it was just fun.

I guess maybe around Homestead I was known as the local whatever, you know. But that was, as far as that went, and I had no idea that I'd ever wind up singing professionally. I just loved the theatre, I loved music. I tried to dance. I think I was somewhat of a jitter-bug. In fact, I mean earlier, in the early twenties, twenty-five, I participated in a Charleston Contest and I won the Charleston Contest over a local winner from way back. And so my prize was an appearance at a local theatre.
